verdicts.title: sqrt() uses assembly stop() for zero input and halts the whole calling transaction

a.reden: Both describe sqrt using stop() for zero input, causing silent halt of execution

b.reden: The candidate describes the same sqrt(0) stop() behavior that halts execution, matching H-02.

verdicts.title: add/sub subtraction path returns a 72-digit mantissa without the L flag for large operands

a.reden: The candidate describes a bug in add()/sub() missing L flag, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes a missing L flag in add/sub subtraction path, which is not covered by any of the known findings (H-01 to H-05).

verdicts.title: ln(0) does not revert and returns a large finite negative number (~ -18,797)

a.reden: Both describe the ln() function lacking validation for zero/non‑positive inputs, leading to incorrect results instead of reverting.

b.reden: The candidate describes the same root cause as H-3: ln() does not revert on zero input and returns an incorrect finite value.

verdicts.title: ln() ignores the sign bit, so ln(-x) silently returns ln(x)

a.reden: Both describe the ln() function failing to validate the sign bit, allowing negative inputs to be processed silently.

b.reden: Both findings describe that ln() does not validate negative inputs, allowing ln(-x) to return ln(x) instead of reverting.

verdicts.title: sqrt() high-exponent path halves an odd pre-exponent after incrementing it, giving a result off by 10x

a.reden: The candidate describes a different exponent handling bug in sqrt than the early 72-digit adjustment covered by H-01

b.reden: Both describe the same exponent calculation error in sqrt when handling large exponents and odd pre-exponent.

verdicts.title: Non-canonical float encodings: L/M boundary off-by-one and inconsistent normalization break raw eq()

a.reden: The candidate describes encoding uniqueness and off‑by‑one normalization issues across eq/add/sub/toPackedFloat, which differ from the specific sqrt, ln, flag handling, or toPackedFloat exponent‑only

b.reden: The candidate describes a different root cause (non-canonical encodings in eq/add/sub/toPackedFloat) than any known finding, which focus on sqrt, ln, eq unwrapping, and precision loss in toPackedFloat

verdicts.title: ln() truncates large-mantissa (L) inputs ≥1 to 38 digits, losing the precision the docs promise

a.reden: The candidate describes a precision loss bug in ln() for large-mantissa inputs, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes a precision loss in ln() for large-mantissa inputs, which is not covered by any of the known findings (H-01 to H-05).

verdicts.title: le()/ge() return false for equal values when mantissa/flag encodings differ (lt/gt reused on tie)

a.reden: The candidate describes a bug in le()/ge() comparison logic, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes a missing non-strict tie case in le()/ge(), while the known findings concern sqrt, ln, eq raw equality, and toPackedFloat precision, not this le/ge flaw.

verdicts.title: No exponent range checks: overflow or underflow of the 14-bit exponent wraps silently and corrupts encoding

a.reden: The candidate describes exponent overflow/underflow in arithmetic functions, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes missing exponent range checks causing silent overflow/underflow, which is not the same root cause as any listed finding.
